The NM4 Hall location is from the 2010 DOE determination, which describes the E906/SeaQuest spectrometer as proposed for that hall; the spectrometer paper (arXiv:1706.09990) describes the instrument itself.
placements.quote: Fermilab proposes to build and operate a spectrometer in the New Muon 4 (NM4) Hall and renovate the 120 giga-electron volt (GeV) beam line from enclosure B to NM4.

summary.plain: The SeaQuest spectrometer used magnets and tracking detectors to catch pairs of muons produced when a proton beam struck hydrogen, deuterium and other targets, revealing the makeup of the proton's antiquark sea.
summary.technical: Dimuon spectrometer: target system, two dipole magnets, four tracking/hodoscope stations and an FPGA trigger, detecting Drell-Yan muon pairs from a 120 GeV proton beam on liquid-hydrogen, liquid-deuterium and solid nuclear targets.

technology.quote: a target system, two dipole magnets and four detector stations
technology.value: Muon spectrometer: a target system followed by two dipole magnets and four detector stations (hodoscopes and tracking chambers) with an FPGA-based trigger, identifying oppositely-charged dimuon pairs from the Drell-Yan process
